chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Halabi from Ayub ibn al-Hurr from Abu Basir said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "There is no harm in the wage of the wailing woman who laments over the deceased."
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And abstaining from that is superior in all cases.
ai.seo_question: Is the wage of a wailing woman permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of paying a professional wailing woman (na'ihah), reflecting the pre-Islamic and early Islamic cultural practice of hired mourners. The addition by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan highlights the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between legal validity (ibahah) and ethical superiority (afdaliyyah), suggesting that while the wage is lawful, voluntary restraint in mourning customs is more virtuous.
